COMPARISON SCOPE. Compared against the entire canonical bank at the represented candidate 78a107f402e33a40dc210635822d8a8314359a9b: 294 question records enumerated from data/questions, 293 compared pairwise against MA-Q-0288. No sampling was used and the existing duplicate report was not relied on. Metrics computed for every pair were stem token Jaccard, whole-item token Jaccard over stem plus all choices, best single-choice token Jaccard, shared rule_ids, and shared area, topic, subtopic, question_type and family_id. Additionally compared against the two exact frozen B3-A R1 repaired variants at c7b438f253089b74231e50040603458d46d20e6c, MA-Q-0241 and MA-Q-0256, as supplemental future-production comparators.

STRONGEST COMPARATORS. (1) MA-Q-0289 is the strongest comparator overall. It is the only bank item sharing a rule_id with MA-Q-0288 (MA-PMP-REGISTRATION-DUTY) and the only other item under topic 'Pharmacist practice'; its subtopic is 'Monitoring program registration' against 'Determinations versus adjacent duties'. Textual overlap is nevertheless low: stem Jaccard 0.035, whole-item Jaccard 0.101, best single-choice Jaccard 0.200. The two items are complementary rather than duplicative. MA-Q-0289 is SBA and tests the substance of the 247 CMR 9.15(1) duty, namely that registration and login maintenance are personal to the dispensing pharmacist and not discharged by the pharmacy's institutional MassPAT account. MA-Q-0288 is SATA and tests the enumerated determination set in 247 CMR 9.15(2), where the monitoring programme appears only as a rejected proposition. A candidate can miss one and answer the other correctly, and the discriminations tested do not overlap. The stems share a stylistic opening ('A newly licensed' against 'A newly hired' Massachusetts pharmacist), noted here for completeness; it is an authoring cadence common to entry-of-practice vignettes and it creates no answer cue, no shared key and no content redundancy. (2) MA-Q-0158 produces the single highest per-choice overlap in the entire bank, best single-choice Jaccard 0.889, arising solely from the recurrence of the statutory formula 'legitimate medical purpose ... usual course of professional practice' in its option E and this item's option B. That formula is a fixed legal phrase that necessarily recurs wherever prescription validity is examined, so its reappearance is unavoidable and correct rather than duplicative. The items are otherwise unrelated: MA-Q-0158 is a federal item in area 3 under rule FED-CII-MULTIPLE testing the multiple Schedule II prescription pathway, quantity limits and earliest-fill-date instructions; MA-Q-0288 is a Massachusetts item in area 2 testing which determinations 247 CMR 9.15(2) enumerates. They share no rule_id, no area, no topic and no subtopic, stem Jaccard is 0.000 and whole-item Jaccard is 0.137. (3) MA-Q-0162 and MA-Q-0163 are the nearest conceptual neighbours, both under 'Prescription validity' with rule FED-CORRESPONDING-RESP. Both are federal corresponding-responsibility items about resolving diversion red flags before a dispensing decision, that is about pharmacist conduct once suspicion arises. MA-Q-0288 asks the prior and different question of which determinations the Massachusetts regulation enumerates at all. Whole-item Jaccard is 0.080 and 0.133 respectively. No collision. Across the full bank the maximum whole-item Jaccard against any question is 0.137 and the maximum stem Jaccard is 0.071, there are no duplicate stems anywhere in the bank, no other question shares this item's family_id B3B_0288R1_MA_VALIDITY_VS_ADJACENT_DUTIES, and no other question contains any choice string identical to any of this item's five choices.

SUPPLEMENTAL B3-A R1 COMPARATORS AT c7b438f253089b74231e50040603458d46d20e6c. MA-Q-0241 (SATA, area 1, 'Pharmacy personnel' / 'Product-specific handling prohibition', rule MA-CII-SUPPORT-HANDLING, concerning a non-abuse-deterrent hydrocodone-only extended release product and support personnel handling) and MA-Q-0256 (SBA, area 1, 'Licensure' / 'Continuing education daily cap', rule MA-CE-ANNUAL-STRUCTURE) are both remote from this item. Whole-item Jaccard is 0.013 and 0.012, stem Jaccard is 0.000 for both, best single-choice Jaccard is 0.000 for both, and neither shares a rule_id, area, topic or subtopic with MA-Q-0288. Neither creates any future-production collision risk.

AUTHENTIC_DISTRACTORS, EXPLICIT PER-OPTION TREATMENT. Both incorrect options state genuine, currently effective Massachusetts obligations that a prepared candidate must actively rule out on legal grounds, which is the standard this criterion sets. Option A, that the prescriber holds a current Massachusetts Controlled Substances Registration: a prepared candidate could very plausibly credit this, and it is the stronger of the two distractors. The governing section is headed 'Verifying a Practitioner's Prescriptive Authority', so a candidate who recalls the heading rather than the enumerated text would expect prescriber-credential verification to be exactly what the section requires the pharmacist to determine. The MCSR is a real and heavily examined Massachusetts credential under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 7, Massachusetts pharmacists do attend to prescriber registration in practice, and the federal corresponding-responsibility framework trains candidates to associate prescriber authority with prescription validity. It is nonetheless wrong because registration verification is not one of the four determinations 247 CMR 9.15(2) enumerates, and within 247 CMR 9.00 the Massachusetts controlled substance registration language attaches to the pharmacy's own maintained documents under 247 CMR 9.19(8), not to any pharmacist determination. Option D, that the patient's history has been screened in the Prescription Monitoring Program: a prepared candidate could also very plausibly credit this. The monitoring-programme duty sits in the immediately preceding subsection, 247 CMR 9.15(1), which is maximal adjacency; MassPAT is highly salient in Massachusetts practice and candidates associate it with pre-dispensing workflow; and several other jurisdictions do impose pharmacist query duties before dispensing, so cross-jurisdictional transfer makes the proposition feel familiar. It is nonetheless wrong because 9.15(1) imposes registration and maintenance of login information, an access obligation, not a determination about the prescription in hand, and because M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 24A directs the utilisation requirement to participants issuing prescriptions while providing for pharmacists to be trained in the programme through continuing education. Neither incorrect option is absurd on its face, neither is a filler, and neither can be eliminated without knowing the boundary of the enumerated list. Correct options B, C and E are not merely plausible but verbatim restatements of 9.15(2)(a), (b) and (c), so the item discriminates on genuine knowledge of the enumeration.

WORDING_NOT_GUESSABLE, EXPLICIT TREATMENT. No surface strategy recovers the key. Length gives no signal in either direction: the correct set contains both the longest option, B at 136 characters and 21 words, and the shortest option, E at 35 characters and 5 words, while the two incorrect options are tightly clustered at 84 and 85 characters. The correct mean length, 75.7 characters, is lower than the incorrect mean, 84.5, so 'longest is correct' and 'shortest is filler' both fail. No option contains an absolute or hedging qualifier: a scan for always, never, only, solely, automatically, immediately, exclusively and all returned zero hits across all five options, so the classical eliminate-the-absolute heuristic yields nothing. All five options are grammatically parallel, each opening as a 'That ...' clause, so no option is a syntactic outlier and none is grammatically mismatched to the stem. The stem does not disclose how many options are correct, and the keyed count of three sits on the bank's modal SATA count, 56 of 112 SATA items key three options, so count-guessing gains nothing. The keyed combination BCE occurs 3 times among 112 SATA items and is not a positional outlier; SATA answer-position load across the bank is spread at A 22.4 percent, B 23.2, C 20.7, D 18.4 and E 15.3. The one surface pattern a test-wise candidate might notice, that the keyed options assert facts about the prescription and the treatment relationship while the rejected options assert external verification acts, is the substantive legal distinction the item is designed to test, namely determinations versus adjacent administrative duties, so exploiting it requires the underlying knowledge rather than substituting for it.

DISTINCT_FROM_BANK, EXPLICIT TREATMENT. Distinct on every measure applied across all 293 comparisons. The item is the sole occupant of its family_id, the sole occupant of its subtopic, and shares its topic with only MA-Q-0289, from which it is separated by question type, by rule focus and by the direction of the discrimination tested. Maximum whole-item overlap anywhere in the bank is 0.137 and maximum stem overlap is 0.071, both low. The single elevated per-choice figure, 0.889 against MA-Q-0158, is fully accounted for by a fixed statutory phrase and is not a content collision. No duplicate stem exists in the bank and no choice string is reused. The tested proposition, that 247 CMR 9.15(2) is a closed enumeration from which two genuinely adjacent Massachusetts duties are absent, is asked nowhere else in the bank.

STEM READING. The stem admits no second reasonable legal reading. 'The regulation' is uniquely fixed by the surrounding words 'requires of her professional judgment before any prescription may be filled', which track the operative language of 247 CMR 9.15(2) and match no competing Massachusetts provision. 'Among the determinations' is necessary and correctly drafted, because the fourth enumerated determination under 9.15(2)(d) is not offered as a choice; the stem therefore does not represent the offered set as exhaustive and cannot be attacked for the omission. 'Before any prescription may be filled' faithfully reproduces the unrestricted scope of 'may not fill a prescription' and does not improperly narrow the rule to controlled substances or improperly widen it beyond filling.

REMAINING CRITERIA. jurisprudence_reasoning: the item requires distinguishing the boundary of an enumerated regulatory list from obligations in the immediately surrounding subsections and section heading, which is reasoning about the scope of an enumeration rather than recall. practice_plausibility: a newly licensed pharmacist asking a preceptor what she must satisfy herself of before filling is an ordinary and realistic entry-of-practice exchange. reasoning_not_trivia: no number, date, threshold or list position is being recalled; the discrimination is which obligations are determinations at all. natural_rule_combination: MA-PRESCRIPTION-VALIDITY-DETERMINATION and MA-PMP-REGISTRATION-DUTY are adjacent subsections of the same section, 247 CMR 9.15(2) and 9.15(1), so combining them reproduces the structure of the regulation itself rather than assembling an artificial pairing. appropriate_drug_context: the rule is drug-agnostic, no drug is named, none is required, and drug_ids is correctly empty. not_schedule_flashcard: no schedule classification, schedule-specific limit or scheduling recall is involved anywhere in the item. public_style_without_copying: the vignette framing, the preceptor exchange and the distractor construction are original; the correct options necessarily track regulatory wording because they restate the enumerated determinations, which is proper restatement of public law and not reproduction of any published examination item.

COMPLETENESS CHECK. Consistent with the independence requirement, the legal and realism judgments recorded above were formed in full before any prior audit finding, repair rationale or old-hash history for MA-Q-0288 was consulted; the Phase-1 blind lock at commit b78ba8ae3b78852a90c92983c5f9b48084db407e independently produced the keyed set B, C, E and rejected A and D before the canonical record was opened. Only afterwards was the superseded item at hash 343520a4112cde0f746b9d4fb5062cc627d25438c3d94e312c5d97759a58bb68 and the prior CLAUDE-FRESH-B3B initial realism finding examined, solely to confirm that nothing previously identified remains unaddressed. That prior finding recorded REALISM FAIL, MINOR_EDIT, Medium, with authentic_distractors false, on two grounds: first, that under the superseded key the item's only incorrect option had no regulatory nexus and no prepared candidate would credit it, so the whole discriminating power rested on a single inauthentic distractor; second, that the superseded stem, which asked what remained to be determined after the prescriber had confirmed authorship by telephone, supported a second reasonable reading on which the authenticity determination had been discharged. Both defects are resolved in the item under review, and my independent analysis reached that conclusion on its own terms before the prior finding was read. The telephone-confirmation clause is gone, and the present stem asks the unconditioned question of what the regulation requires before any prescription may be filled, which as recorded above admits no second reasonable legal reading. The single inauthentic distractor is gone and has been replaced by two independently authentic ones, options A and D, each a genuine and currently effective Massachusetts obligation drawn from the section heading and from the immediately preceding subsection respectively, each analysed per-option above. The keyed set moved from four correct of five to three correct of five, so discriminating power now rests on two authentic rejections rather than one implausible one. No residual defect from the prior finding survives, and this review identifies no new defect. Contamination status CLEAN.
